recent_posts.title: The Quiet Shift: How AI Is Reshaping Product Work — Kogan.com Dev Blog
recent_posts.summary: A product manager at Kogan.com shares how AI has become embedded in day-to-day product work across five areas: scheduled background automations (ticket triage, squad reports, stakeholder updates via Claude Cowork), customer session analysis using FullStory, meeting capture with Granola, team skill building through reusable prompt patterns, and direct codebase exploration. The author also describes personally implementing tickets using Claude Code and Cursor despite limited development background, freeing engineering capacity and deepening system understanding. A practical three-part test (repetitive, mundane, not decision-driven) is offered to identify automation candidates, with the overall message that AI reduces coordination friction without displacing core product judgment.

recent_posts.title: What Sets the Kogan.com Engineering Culture Apart — Kogan.com Dev Blog
recent_posts.summary: Kogan.com engineers describe their engineering culture through three first-person perspectives. Key themes include strong ownership (engineers are accountable end-to-end for reliability, security, and maintainability), fast iteration (daily deployments, small tickets, just-in-time planning), cross-functional collaboration with product/design/data teams, and sustainable practices like the Boy Scout Rule and 'Ship Frenzy' cleanup sessions. AI tools are used to boost productivity but engineers remain accountable for all decisions. The culture prioritizes measurable impact over completed tickets and treats code as a long-term asset.

recent_posts.title: Improving Frontend Regression Testing with Chromatic — Kogan.com Dev Blog
recent_posts.summary: Kogan.com integrated Chromatic for visual regression testing after migrating to Remix to catch UI changes that unit tests miss. The implementation leverages existing Storybook stories and includes an automated pipeline that generates API mocks from OpenAPI schemas, keeping stories synchronized with backend contracts. Chromatic runs visual comparisons in CI during pull requests, surfacing UI changes for explicit approval. Key learnings include the importance of good Storybook coverage, baseline discipline, and treating visual testing as part of a broader strategy rather than a standalone solution.

recent_posts.title: Patterns & Best Practices in Event-Driven Systems — Kogan.com Dev Blog
recent_posts.summary: Event-driven architecture enables decoupled, scalable systems through five core patterns: event notification (lightweight signals), event-carried state transfer (self-contained payloads), event sourcing (immutable change logs), choreography (decentralized workflows), and orchestration (centralized coordination). Essential practices include implementing idempotency to handle duplicate events, using durable message streams for replay capability, versioning events explicitly, managing schemas through registries, naming events after business domain concepts, and tracking requests with correlation IDs for distributed debugging and observability.

recent_posts.title: Moving from Django DRF to Ninja API
recent_posts.summary: Kogan.com's engineering team shares their experience migrating from Django REST Framework to Django Ninja API with Pydantic. The shift reduces boilerplate code, improves type safety through Python type hints, and provides automatic OpenAPI documentation. The post includes practical code examples comparing DRF's serializer-based approach with Ninja's schema-based pattern, demonstrating how Pydantic models handle both validation and serialization. Key benefits include clearer code structure, better developer experience, and improved maintainability, though the transition requires adapting to new patterns and considering ecosystem maturity.

recent_posts.title: Four Years Strong: Celebrating Our Koganniversaries — Kogan.com Dev Blog
recent_posts.summary: Three engineers at Kogan.com share their experiences after four years with the company, discussing career progression from individual contributor to tech lead roles. They highlight key technical achievements including OpenSearch performance optimization (20% latency reduction through smaller shards), product listing page improvements, and a hybrid search experiment that prioritized business metrics over technical novelty. The interviews emphasize the importance of tying engineering work to measurable business outcomes and the value of collaborative team environments for career growth.

recent_posts.title: Building Your Own AI Agent — Kogan.com Dev Blog
recent_posts.summary: AI agents are surprisingly simple to build, consisting of just a few hundred lines of code running in a loop with LLM tokens. The core concept involves moving from using generative AI as a tool to building complete agentic systems that can autonomously reason, plan, and execute actions. The fundamental architecture includes an inferencing loop that processes user input, analyzes responses, and executes tools when needed. Five key primitives enable coding agents: read, list, bash, edit, and search tools. Engineers should embrace building these systems to become producers of automation rather than just consumers, as this skill will be crucial for career development in the AI era.

recent_posts.title: Order Dispatch Systems at Scale — Kogan.com Dev Blog
recent_posts.summary: Explores scaling strategies for order dispatch systems using restaurant analogies. Compares vertical vs horizontal scaling approaches, discusses the evolution from queue-based systems (AWS SQS) to event-driven architecture (AWS EventBridge). Highlights the importance of identifying external bottlenecks like SAP's single-threaded API and upgrading to more scalable alternatives like the Service Layer. Emphasizes that proper architectural design is crucial for handling increased load and system growth.

recent_posts.title: Empowering Data Through Self-Service: Behind the Scenes of Our Data Platform — Kogan.com Dev Blog
recent_posts.summary: Kogan.com transformed their data platform from a request-based Tableau model to a self-service architecture using dbt, Looker, and Acryl DataHub. The new platform features modular data flows with layered dbt modeling, governed exploration through Looker's LookML, and comprehensive metadata management via DataHub. Key improvements include version-controlled business logic, CI/CD pipelines, row-level security, and AI-powered natural language queries. The migration process involves not just recreating dashboards but improving data models and user experience. The platform emphasizes governance through transparency rather than restrictions, enabling teams to explore data independently while maintaining trust and quality.

recent_posts.title: Beyond the Code: Threat Modeling as Your Security Superpower — Kogan.com Dev Blog
recent_posts.summary: Threat modeling serves as a proactive security tool for developers. It involves anticipating potential threats from an attacker's perspective to identify vulnerabilities in the software design. The process includes mapping out assets, anticipating attacks using frameworks like STRIDE, implementing controls to mitigate threats, and regularly updating threat models to adapt to evolving systems. Threat modeling enhances security, reduces vulnerabilities, and aligns with compliance needs.
